name: Waakye (Ghanian Rice and Beans)
author: Wikibooks Cookbook contributors

ingredients.item: 3–4 leaves of Guinea corn leaves, washed
1 milk tin (14 fl oz) beans, washed
2 milk tins (28 fl oz) brown or white rice, washed

steps: Half-fill a saucepan with water, and place over the fire. Add the Guinea corn leaves.
Bring to a boil, and add the beans.
Simmer for 40-45 minutes until the beans split in two when touched.
Add the rice and salt, and simmer until the beans and rice are very soft. Add additional water as necessary during the cooking.
Remove from the heat. Serve with shito and fried tomato stew, accompanied by wele, tilapia, boiled eggs, and salad.

culture.text: Waakye is a Ghanaian dish of cooked rice and beans, commonly eaten for breakfast or lunch. Rice and beans, usually black eyed peas or cow beans, are cooked together, along with red dried sorghum leaf sheaths or stalks and kaun. The sorghum leaves and limestone give the dish its characteristic flavor and a red appearance and the sorghum is taken out before consumption. The word waakye is from the Dagbani language and refers to a particular kind of bean. In Hausa, the bean and the dish are called wake, a contracted form of the full name shinkafa da wake which means rice and beans.
